highlightAliases.old: AAA means over 50% vessel-diameter enlargement, generally above 3 cm in men. It may remain silent until expansion or rupture (p1214).
highlightAliases.new: An abdominal aortic aneurysm is usually defined on ultrasound by an infrarenal aortic diameter ≥3.0 cm or an enlargement at least 50% above the expected diameter. It can remain silent until expansion or rupture (p1214, USPSTF AAA screening recommendation).

highlightAliases.old: Repair is generally considered above 5–5.5 cm; endovascular repair has short-term advantages, but long-term outcomes can resemble open repair (p1210).
highlightAliases.new: For an unruptured AAA, ACC/AHA recommends repair at a maximal diameter ≥5.5 cm in men or ≥5.0 cm in women. Symptoms attributable to the aneurysm or rapid growth may warrant earlier repair. Endovascular repair can have short-term benefits, with later outcomes dependent on anatomy, follow-up and reintervention (p1210).

highlightAliases.old: Antiplatelet treatment and a high-potency statin address vascular risk. Cilostazol may improve claudication distance; use caution with heart failure (p1211).
highlightAliases.new: Antiplatelet treatment and a high-potency statin address vascular risk. Cilostazol may improve claudication distance and is contraindicated in heart failure of any severity (p1211 and 2024 ACC/AHA PAD guideline, section 5.7).
